findings.decisive_proof: P(|alpha_j|>eps)=(1-eps^2)^(beta(j+1)/2) is summable. Borel-Cantelli gives alpha_j->0 a.s. CMV block differences from the free blocks tend to zero, hence tail operator norm tends to zero. The free odd-chain vectors N^(-1/2)sum_{k=J}^{J+N-1}zeta^(-k)e_{2k+1} have squared residual 2/N for every |zeta|=1. They give Weyl sequences for the perturbed matrix by sending J,N to infinity. Cyclic spectral support is the spectrum, hence the full circle.

independent_verification.assumptions: Choose beta=4, within the subcritical range, with exactly the independent rotationally invariant alpha_j satisfying |alpha_j|^2~Beta(1,2(j+1)); the limiting measure is the cyclic CMV spectral measure of this sequence. No atypical deterministic coefficient sequence is substituted.
independent_verification.independent_proof: Integrating the beta density gives P(|alpha_j|>epsilon)=(1-epsilon^2)^(beta(j+1)/2); its geometric sum is finite for every 0<epsilon<1 and beta>0. Applying Borel-Cantelli to a countable epsilon sequence gives alpha_j->0 almost surely. The two-by-two block differences from the zero-coefficient blocks converge to zero in norm, so L-L_free and M-M_free, and hence LM-L_free M_free, are compact. In zero-based indexing M_free sends e_(2k+1) to e_(2k+2), and L_free sends that to e_(2k+3). For arbitrary |zeta|=1, v=N^(-1/2) sum_(k=J)^(J+N-1) zeta^(-k)e_(2k+1) has only two nonzero residual coefficients under (C_free-zeta), each of modulus N^(-1/2), giving exact squared residual 2/N. Letting N increase and the starting position J escape makes both residual and compact-perturbation error vanish. Every point of the circle is spectral; unitarity confines the spectrum to that circle. Cyclic spectral representation identifies spectrum with closed support. Thus the topological support has dimension 1 almost surely, whereas beta=4 gives the printed 1/2 and beta=2 gives 0.
independent_verification.counterevidence: A dense full-measure carrier can have smaller Hausdorff dimension than its closure. The proof does not refute the intended measure dimension or the main random-measure correspondence. The source search contexts contain no stated unconventional support definition that would resolve the literal notation.
independent_verification.impact: The object whose dimension is asserted in a consequence requires clarification. It is a Minor formulation correction with a demonstrated difference for the actual probability law.
independent_verification.repair: Replace the topological-support notation by an explicitly defined measure dimension, for example inf{dim_H E:E Borel, mu(E)=1}, and identify exactly the dimensional conclusion supplied by the cited spectral result.
independent_verification.repair_limits: The value for this replacement object, stronger exact-dimensionality, and the source's extension of Simon's hypotheses are not independently proved here. Initial search obtained a contents page rather than the full cited theorem; no fabricated acquisition is recorded.

findings.decisive_independent_calculation: Set I_t=integral_0^t 4(1-X_u)/(beta*u)du. The stated near-zero assumption gives 0<=I_t<=8*C(omega)*sqrt(t)/beta for small t. Therefore I_t->0 a.s., P(I_t<=alpha)->1 and P(I_t>=alpha)->0. The printed lower-tail event cannot be discarded to obtain the next limsup estimate. The upper-tail event on p.67 supplies exactly the needed estimate.
findings.impact: Local sign/transcription correction; the preceding correct tail split restores this inference with the same assumptions. No new substantive failure of the limiting law or main theorem is established.
findings.repair: Replace <= alpha inside the first probability on p.68 by >= alpha, as on p.67. The t->0 limit then kills that probability; alpha->0 kills the Brownian supremum tail.

independent_verification.assumptions: beta>2; continuous X solves the specified SDE in [0,1]; for every epsilon_0 in (0,1), (1-X_t)/t^(1-epsilon_0) is almost surely bounded near zero; alpha>0 is fixed before t decreases to zero.
independent_verification.independent_proof: Choose epsilon_0=1/2. On each path in the probability-one event, 0<=1-X_u<=C(omega)sqrt(u) near zero, with finite C. Direct integration gives 0<=I_t=integral_0^t 4(1-X_u)/(beta u)du<=8C(omega)sqrt(t)/beta->0. For each fixed alpha>0, the lower-tail indicator tends to one and the upper-tail indicator to zero; bounded convergence gives P(I_t<=alpha)->1 and P(I_t>=alpha)->0. Thus the printed lower-tail probability cannot be discarded to infer the displayed limsup bound.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The previous page already contains the correct upper-tail event. The issue does not furnish a counterexample to the entrance law or the main identification.
independent_verification.impact: A local transcription/sign error in this passage, with a complete correction using the unchanged assumptions.
independent_verification.repair: Use I_t>=alpha in the p.68 first probability as on p.67. Its probability vanishes as t->0; the remaining P(sqrt(alpha)V>=a) vanishes as alpha->0 since V is finite almost surely.
independent_verification.repair_limits: This repairs this limiting inequality only and does not certify every other diffusion or Dufresne argument.
